chunks: The Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Abān, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a dog drinking from a vessel. He said: Wash the vessel. And about the cat, he said: There is no problem in performing wudu (ablution) from what remains of it; it is only one of the beasts.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a dog or a cat drinks from a vessel?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling concerning water and vessels from which animals have drunk. It distinguishes between the dog, whose drinking necessitates washing the vessel, and the cat, from whose leftover water wudu (ablution) may still be performed.
